UAE Awards $285M EPC Contract for Desalination Plant P3 Project
By Shem Oirere
Photo courtesy EtihadWE
Officials of Etihad Water and Electricity, and contractors Lantania and NMDC ink Fujairah desalination plant project agreement.
June 11, 2026
The United Arab Emirates state-owned water utility firm, Etihad Water and Electricity, has awarded a $285-million engineering, procurement and construction contract to build a seawater reverse osmosis desalination plant—the second one to be delivered under a public private partnership model in the country.
The utility has picked UAE-based NMDC Infra and Spain-based Lantania Aguas, through their joint venture called JV Lantania NMDC Water, to develop the Fujairah I Independent Water Producer project, a 272,765 cu-meter-per-day desalination facility. The project is set to be completed in 30 months to boost the country's Water Security Strategy 2036, a national plan to achieve sustainable and continuous access to an adequate drinking water supply.
The project, being developed at the Port of Fujairah about 75 miles northeast of the city of Dubai on the Persian Gulf, will have storage capacity equivalent to 18 hours of production. It will draw in seawater and remove salt and impurities to produce potable water for residential, commercial and industrial uses, according to the utility.
The project will have a seawater open channel intake, a piped outfall, reverse osmosis plant and potable water storage tanks, although Etihad Water and Electricity has yet to confirm the dimensions or specific details of these components.
Utility CEO Mohammed Al Shehhi said the project "marks an important step in [its] journey ... to develop [reverse osmosis] capacity across its network.”
The company, which delivers electricity and water services in six emirates, is expected to sign a long-term water supply agreement with Lantania NMDC Water. The project "will add important investment value to the utility portfolio," said the CEO, adding that the company is currently developing multiple projects to be announced.
NMDC Group had in January, through its subsidiary NMDC Infra, acquired a 51% majority stake in Lantana Aguas, a specialized desalination, water treatment and purification affiliate of Lantana Group.
The Fujairah project is the second desalination project being procured by the utility in using the public-private partnership model—after the $800-million Naqa’a facility located about 124 miles north of Abu Dhabi, with production capacity of more than 681,900 cubic meters per day.

Home / Products / Plant engineering / Industrial service & maintenance
Industrial service & maintenance
Our service for you
Even after the successful commissioning of your plant, BUTTING is your reliable service provider for industrial services. During maintenance, we provide you with technical advice, also with regard to the subsequent adaptation of the systems to new requirements, thus ensuring optimum performance of the system parts and components.
With in-depth expertise and many years of experience, we are committed to the success of your plant thanks to our large number of qualified employees. We guarantee
minimisation of downtimes during maintenance
short response times thanks to an extensive warehouse and
reliability and expertise in every respect.
In demand worldwide
BUTTING offers you "everything from a single source" when it comes to plant construction. This bundles responsibility and increases the economic efficiency of your project. You benefit from the powerful network of the BUTTING Group. With production sites in Germany, China and Finland as well as representative offices in Canada and Brazil, among others, we can fulfil your project-specific requirements worldwide, if required.
The use of complex welding techniques, the processing of special materials and the manufacture of stainless steel pipes have always been our core competences. In addition, we offer you customised solutions for piping systems, vessels and columns made of nickel-based alloys, duplex and super-duplex materials and clad materials.

Pembina selects Worley to deliver Heartland Extraction Plant in Alberta
August 11, 2026 • 1 min read
Pembina selects Worley to deliver Heartland Extraction Plant in Alberta
Worley has been awarded a contract by Pembina Pipeline Corporation (Pembina) to provide engineering, procurement, fabrication and construction (EPC) services for the Heartland Extraction Plant (HEP) in Strathcona County, Alberta, Canada.
The Heartland Extraction Plant is a greenfield straddle facility designed to process up to 750 million cubic feet per day of natural gas. The facility will extract natural gas liquids (NGL) from the Yellowhead Pipeline and is scheduled to begin operations in late 2029.
The project will be delivered by an integrated EPC team from Worley’s Alberta locations.
“This award is further evidence of Worley’s expertise in delivering integrated gas projects and continues our long-standing relationship with Pembina, reflecting their ongoing confidence in Worley as a full project delivery partner,” said Chris Ashton, Chief Executive Officer.

Contract workers’ strike at Visakhapatnam Steel Plant: Human Rights Forum condemns privatization push, demands immediate reinstatement
Nalla Babu / TNN / May 29, 2025, 15:41 IST
Share
AA
+Text Size
Small
Medium
Large
The Human Rights Forum (HRF) supports the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant's contract workers' strike against unfair treatment and terminations due to privatization policies. HRF condemns the management's intimidation tactics and demands the reinstatement of 3,000 terminated workers, opposing the government's privatization efforts of the plant built on significant local sacrifice. They call for peaceful resolution and halt to privatization.
VISAKHAPATNAM: The Human Rights Forum (HRF) stands in solidarity with the ongoing agitation by contract workers of the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant. Contract workers at the VSP have been on an indefinite strike for the past 10 days to realise their legitimate rights in the face of sustained threats by the management.The HRF, led by KV Jagannadha Rao, HRF AP State President, and VS Krishna, HRF AP and TG Coordination Committee member, demands that the 3,000 contract workers who were recently terminated under the govt’s retrograde privatisation policies be reinstated immediately. The management must abandon attempts to terminate a further 1,800 contract workers.We condemn the management’s use of police to intimidate workers instead of engaging in dialogue and seeking a democratic resolution of issues raised by them. Resorting to fear tactics instead of negotiation, particularly when production at the plant is being affected, is unacceptable. Contract workers are the backbone of daily operations at the plant, but they continue to be denied basic rights, job security, and dignity at the workplace. Their persistent demands for regularisation and fair wages are met not with dialogue, but with intimidation and removal.It is common knowledge that the central govt is orchestrating a systematic conspiracy to privatise the steel plant by sanitising its financials—issuing an Rs 11,440 crore package, waiving GST and other dues, and making the plant attractive for private players.
We condemn this attempt to hand over a precious industrial asset—built on the sacrifice of 32 lives and the voluntary land donation by people of 69 villages—to corporate interests on a platter.In the 40-year history of the VSP, we have not witnessed such intimidation tactics and huge police deployment. The suspension of protesting workers and the issuance of show-cause notices, we believe, are in direct violation of the Industrial Disputes Act of 1948. These actions are nothing but the implementation of the regressive new labour codes that the govt is actively pushing.HRF calls for the immediate stoppage of punitive actions by the management and a democratic and peaceful resolution of grievances of employees and contract workers at the VSP. All attempts to privatise the steel plant must be halted.

Petroleum Refining
Consumers' Co-operative Refineries Moves Forward with $1.9 Billion Refinery Expansion in Canada
CCRL has selected International Alliance Group (Houston, Texas) as the project management contractor for the construction of the new units and ...
Released Wednesday, March 05, 2008
Researched by Industrial Info Resources (Sugar Land, Texas)--Consumers' Co-operative Refineries Limited (CCRL) is progressing with its $1.9 billion refinery expansion in Regina, Saskatchewan. The project will increase the refinery's capacity by 30% to 130,000 barrels per day (BPD) to process additional crude oil. Construction is expected to begin in early 2009 and finish by 2011. CCRL has selected International Alliance Group (Houston, Texas) as the project management contractor for the construction of the new units and Mustang Engineering (Houston) to perform engineering and procurement for the new units. Colt Engineering (Markham, Ontario) is performing engineering, procurement and construction for the revamp units involved with the expansion.
The expansion will involve several new units: 30,000 BPD fluid catalytic cracker unit, polymerization unit, merox unit and offsite utilities work. In addition, the revamp will include modifications to the distillate hydrotreater, hydrocracker unit, reformer, gasoline hydrotreater, isomerization unit and saturated gas unit. The existing processing units will be revamped to give the unit a higher throughput. The total investment to modify the existing units will be an estimated $400 million.
CCRL was founded in April 1934. CCRL is a subsidiary of Federated Co-operative Limited (FCL), which owns and operates the refinery in Saskatchewan. The refinery employs more than 530 employees and is located on 544 acres of land in North Regina. The refinery upgrader complex currently processes about 100,000 BPD of crude oil.
